name: crypto-chacha20poly1305
algorithm: std ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) seal then open of every 16,384-byte record of splitmix64 bytes, a fresh nonce per record, a 13-byte aad, reps passes (mk/crypto-chacha20poly1305.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard AEAD
skip.go: no exported ChaCha20-Poly1305 in Go std: it is vendor/golang.org/x/crypto, importable only by std itself; x/crypto is not std
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no AEAD; no crate stands in

notes: Work per step: one seal and one open of one 16,384-byte record with a 13-byte aad, the tag checked before decryption on both sides. Mk ChaCha20Poly1305.Seal and Open, Zig aead.chacha_poly.ChaCha20Poly1305.encrypt and decrypt. Go's std has no exported ChaCha20-Poly1305 (golang.org/x/crypto is not std). Bytes per second = 2 * mib * 1048576 * reps / median (each byte is sealed and opened).
Zig: std.crypto ChaCha20 uses @Vector lanes (several blocks at once); Mk's is scalar, one block at a time (std-vector's rewrite).

Checksums: every column printed the same value at the quick and the publish args in `go run ./tools/bench verify` and `verify -publish-size` (mk built from the tree, Zig 0.17.0, Go 1.27.3) on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07 (std-crypto session 1). Not published: no number here is a measurement.
